evaluated.name: CashEbitdaYieldBSAccrual
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: An operating-earnings yield built from EBITDA net of the balance-sheet working-capital accrual is a cleaner measure of distributable cash cheapness than any accounting-earnings yield.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of ranking two separate channels, this embeds the Sloan-style balance-sheet accrual directly inside the numerator of the valuation ratio, so a firm looks cheap only if its operating profit is not financed by receivable/inventory build-ups. The balance-sheet accrual construction is independent of cash-flow-statement reporting conventions, giving a different measurement path than signals 1-3.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SalesYieldReceivableBacked
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(recch, 0), COALESCE(invch, 0)), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: Sales-based cheapness is trustworthy only when revenue is converted into cash rather than parked in receivables and inventory.
evaluated.reasoning: Sales-to-price avoids earnings management in the denominator of profitability but is vulnerable to channel-stuffing; recch and invch (cash-flow-statement decreases in receivables/inventory, positive when working capital releases cash) test exactly that conversion. COALESCE to zero is justified because an unreported working-capital line item means no disclosed change, not a missing firm.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ValueWithWorkingCapitalDiscipline
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheap firms are rewarded when revenue is being generated with shrinking (not expanding) non-cash working capital, because a rising working-capital intensity of sales is the balance-sheet footprint of soft revenue recognition and predicts earnings reversal.
evaluated.reasoning: The valuation channel (book-to-market) and the accrual channel (change in non-cash working capital per dollar of sales) share no variable, so the composite genuinely combines two independent sources of information rather than re-deriving CFO/P from oancf twice. Scaling working capital by sales rather than assets makes the accrual leg a revenue-quality measure, distinguishing operationally lean cheap firms from cheap firms whose reported growth is trapped in receivables and inventory.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWeightedAccrualQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among cheap firms, the return spread is driven by whether reported profits are backed by cash rather than by working-capital build-up; cheapness itself should act as an amplifier of the accrual effect, not as the sorting variable.
evaluated.reasoning: The centered accrual-quality rank supplies the cross-sectional dispersion while RANK(book-to-market) only scales its magnitude, so the long and short legs hold comparably cheap firms and the spread is close to HML-neutral — exactly the flaw that made gen-0 FF5 alphas negative. Economically it implements the value-trap story literally: long cheap-and-cash-backed, short cheap-and-accrual-financed, with glamour firms parked near zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithConservativeDepreciation
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is trustworthy when the firm charges heavy depreciation relative to its asset base for its industry, because aggressive capitalization and stretched useful lives inflate book earnings and book equity, producing artificial cheapness.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the working-capital accrual channel with a long-lived-asset accrual channel (depreciation adequacy), which is the second and largely independent component of total accruals, and industry-ranking removes the capital-intensity confound that would otherwise make dp/at an industry bet. Like Signal 1 it keeps both legs equally cheap, so any alpha should be residual to HML rather than a repackaged value premium.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithFallingWorkingCapitalTrend
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A multi-year upward drift in working capital per dollar of sales reveals a slow, persistent accrual build that one-year accrual measures miss; cheap firms with such a drift are value traps, while cheap firms tightening working capital are genuine bargains.
evaluated.reasoning: The economic content is a state variable (chronic deterioration of operating discipline) rather than a single-year flow, which should be less noisy and less mechanically reversing than DELTA-based accruals, so it isolates whether persistence or timing carries the information. It shares the conditioning architecture of Signal 1 deliberately, so the comparison cleanly identifies the value of the temporal dimension.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashEbitdaToEnterpriseValue
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-converted operating profit should be priced against the whole capital structure; the accrual-adjusted operating yield is informative about mispricing only once the leverage tilt in an equity-only deflator is removed.
evaluated.reasoning: This directly addresses the critic's objection to the gen-0 winner: an unlevered numerator over levered equity value created a leverage bet that plausibly contributed to the negative FF5 alpha, since leverage correlates with HML and CMA loadings. Keeping everything else identical makes the enterprise-value deflator a clean, single-design-choice test of whether the negative alpha was a leverage artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithLowAccrualOpacity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: For cheap stocks it is the *magnitude* of the non-cash working-capital swing, in either direction, that signals unreliable accounting; large absolute accruals mean the reported number is an estimate rather than a realization, so cheapness is only credible when the accrual footprint is small.
evaluated.reasoning: Dropping depreciation from the numerator removes the capital-intensity dominance the critic identified, and taking ABS makes this an accounting-opacity (information-risk) channel that is non-monotone in signed accruals, so it is not the published price-scaled accrual measure nor a restatement of the accepted signed-accrual signals. Keeping cheapness as a multiplicative weight on a centered rank means both legs hold comparably cheap firms, so any alpha is residual to HML rather than a repackaged value premium.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ValueRankMigrationOnCashEarnings
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is whether a firm still looks cheap after its earnings are restated onto a cash basis: firms that climb the earnings-yield ranking under the accrual adjustment are genuinely cheap, while firms that fall down the ranking only appeared cheap because accruals inflated reported income.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the additive two-anomaly stack with a within-firm comparison of two valuation percentiles, so the level of cheapness differences out and the surviving variation is purely the accrual content of the earnings the market is capitalizing — an explicit interaction rather than a sum of separate effects. Measuring the shift in percentile units (not in accrual dollars per share price) normalizes for local density of the value distribution, avoids the dividend-payer tie mass, and keeps coverage as broad as the standard earnings-yield sample.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapFallingNoncashWCTrend
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A multi-year rise in *non-cash* working capital per dollar of sales is the signature of a chronic accrual build; cheap firms with that drift are value traps, while cheap firms whose non-cash working capital is shrinking relative to sales have cash-validated cheapness.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the one clear portfolio winner by removing cash and short-term debt from the accrual leg, so a cheap firm accumulating cash is no longer mislabeled as accrual-financed — the exact contradiction the critic identified. Everything else (conditional architecture, 5-year trend, cheapness weight) is held fixed, making this a clean test of whether cleaning the accrual definition strengthens both the FMB slope and the alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithRisingDepreciationIntensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The long-lived-asset accrual channel works through depreciation adequacy: firms that let depreciation intensity drift down are stretching useful lives and capitalizing costs to prop up book earnings, so their cheapness is manufactured, whereas cheap firms with rising depreciation intensity are recognizing costs conservatively.
evaluated.reasoning: It resurrects the depreciation channel that scored highest with the critic but died at 0% coverage because industry operators are unavailable in this environment; using a within-firm 5-year trend instead of IND_RANK removes the capital-intensity confound through the firm's own history rather than through peers. This is the only proposal that sources accrual quality outside working capital, so it diversifies the archive's dominant channel.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapCashFlowNotPayableFunded
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(apalch, 0), COALESCE(txach, 0)), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Even cash-flow-based cheapness can be fake: operating cash flow inflated by stretching payables and deferring tax remittances is borrowed liquidity, not earned cash, so cheap-on-CFO firms whose CFO is funded by payable and tax accruals underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This attacks the one construct the critic said subsumes both themes (CFO/P) by decomposing the *source* of the cash flow, which no archive signal does — the quality leg uses only liability-side cash-flow-statement accruals and is therefore mechanically independent of the receivable/inventory and depreciation channels already tested. COALESCE-to-zero is defensible because an unreported payables or tax-accrual line means no disclosed change in that item.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EarningsYieldWithStableAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: High earnings yield is informative only when the accrual process is stable; erratic year-to-year swings in non-cash working capital intensity indicate estimate-driven, non-persistent earnings, so apparent cheapness on those earnings is unreliable.
evaluated.reasoning: This restores the second-moment idea that the validator rejected earlier for lacking an accruals-exclusive variable, now built from act/lct so it qualifies and is measured on the balance sheet. It is the only proposal keyed to accrual *instability* rather than accrual level or slope, and it pairs with an earnings-yield rather than book-based valuation weight, so it teaches a different lesson than Signals 1-3.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WeakestLinkCheapAndClean
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness and accounting quality are complements with no substitutability: a firm must clear both hurdles to be a genuine bargain, and failing either one is sufficient to disqualify it, so the binding constraint — the weaker of the two percentile scores — should price the stock.
evaluated.reasoning: The MIN operator encodes a conjunctive (Leontief) interaction that is neither a rank sum, a rank product, nor a gate, so the long leg is cheap-and-clean while the short leg contains firms that fail on either dimension — a structurally different portfolio composition from every archive signal. Testing it tells us whether the value-trap mechanism is better described as a joint hurdle than as a continuous weighting, using the accrual channel that has already shown portfolio-level promise.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapAfterAccrualUnwind
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual bloat must eventually reverse through the income statement, so the attractive moment to own a cheap stock is *after* the unwind: firms whose non-cash working capital intensity now sits far below its own five-year peak have already absorbed the earnings hit, leaving depressed reported earnings, a low price, and cash-backed forward earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a genuine new signal rather than a monotone re-scaling: distance-from-own-maximum measures the *state of completion* of the accrual reversal, which is economically and mechanically distinct from a five-year slope (Signal 1), a dispersion measure (Signal 4), or a one-year flow, and it changes the sorted portfolios. It also sharpens the value-trap story into a timing statement — cheapness is safest once the accrual overhang has been worked off — while keeping the HML-neutral conditional architecture that produced the archive's only positive FF5 alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapTwoChannelAccrualState
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Working-capital discipline and depreciation adequacy are two largely independent dimensions of accounting quality, so a cheap firm that scores well on both has genuinely cash-validated cheapness and the combined quality state should predict returns more reliably than either channel alone.
evaluated.reasoning: Both ingredient channels delivered positive but individually imprecise FF5 alphas (t = 2.70 and 1.46) from different parts of the accounting system — current operating assets versus long-lived assets — so averaging their ranks should cancel channel-specific noise and raise both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha rather than just relabel one of them. This is the batch's consolidation move, using the archive as evidence about which channels to combine.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithCumulativeCashConversion
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(SUB(oancf, ib), dp), 5), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting quality is a multi-year property: a cheap firm whose cumulative five-year working-capital accrual (earnings minus cash flow, net of depreciation) is negative has been converting profit into cash for years, whereas a persistent positive cumulative accrual marks earnings that have been borrowed from the future.
evaluated.reasoning: This measures the same "state not flow" insight that made the trend channels work, but via cumulative cash-flow-statement conversion rather than a balance-sheet slope, and removing depreciation prevents the capital-intensity confound the critic raised about dp/at. It is the cleanest available test of whether the persistence of cash backing — rather than its direction of change — is what supports cheapness.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DeepValueOnlyAccrualState
evaluated.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The value-trap mechanism is nonlinear in cheapness: accounting quality matters decisively only where the market is pricing the equity below book value, because that is where the market is implicitly betting the reported earnings will not persist.
evaluated.reasoning: A continuous rank amplifier spreads the interaction over the whole cross-section, whereas the hard price-to-book cutoff concentrates both legs inside the deep-value subsample where the economics bite, and the discarded firms sit at zero in the *middle* of the distribution rather than at an extreme, so breakpoints stay interpretable. It tests convexity of the amplifier, a design dimension the archive has never probed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithTaxVerifiedEarnings
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Income taxes payable are a third-party-verified claim that arises only when profits are real in the tax authority's eyes, so a cheap firm that persistently carries meaningful accrued taxes has earnings validated outside the accounting discretion of management, while a cheap firm reporting book profits with negligible tax liabilities is likely reporting accrual-inflated income.
evaluated.reasoning: This opens the tax channel, which is untouched in the archive and is economically independent of both working-capital slopes and depreciation adequacy — book-tax divergence is the classic external check on earnings quality. The three-year average implements the archive's clearest lesson (multi-year states beat one-year flows) while txp is a densely populated balance-sheet item, so coverage should match the study's norm rather than shrink like the cash-flow-statement lines.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapNotSupplierFinanced
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Conventional accrual measures treat rising operating liabilities as good news (a negative accrual), but for cheap firms a multi-year build-up of non-debt current liabilities per dollar of sales is supplier and tax financing of a strained business, and such firms underperform despite looking cash-generative.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates the *liability side* of the accrual identity — the component that the asset-side channels (receivables, inventory, depreciation) already tested cannot speak to — and it deliberately reverses the sign convention that Sloan-style measures impose, making it a falsifiable economic claim rather than a patch. Unlike the abandoned apalch/txach version it uses densely reported balance-sheet items and changes exactly one thing relative to the archive's trend architecture, so the result is attributable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardAssetBookToMarket
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book equity is a mixture of hard components (cash, long-lived assets) and soft, estimate-laden net working capital (receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities); cheapness backed by hard book value is real, while cheapness backed mostly by soft working capital is an accounting artifact that reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike a three-year accrual haircut, non-cash working capital is typically a large fraction of book equity — often tens of percent, and negative for cash-rich firms — so this construct reorders the value cross-section substantially rather than replicating HML's ranking. It gives the study one non-conditional test whose economic content is the *composition* of book value rather than its level, which is the mechanism by which HML mistakes soft-asset firms for bargains.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ThreeChannelQualityCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting quality supporting cheapness has three separable dimensions — working-capital discipline, depreciation adequacy, and the completed unwinding of past accrual bloat — and a cheap firm scoring well on all three has earnings that are simultaneously cash-converted, conservatively costed, and free of an unreversed overhang.
evaluated.reasoning: Two-channel averaging raised the FF5 alpha from 2.2% to 3.0% and the t-stat from 2.70 to 3.42, so the natural test is whether the third channel that also produced standalone positive alpha (accrual unwind, +1.6%, t 1.85) adds further independent information or is redundant with the working-capital slope. The three legs use different accounting objects (level slope, long-lived-asset charge, distance from own historical peak), so their errors should be weakly correlated.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: QualityCompositeWithTaxCheck
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: External verification by the tax authority is a distinct form of earnings validation from internal cash conversion, so adding persistent accrued taxes to the quality composite should identify cheap firms whose profits are real to both the cash cycle and the taxman.
evaluated.reasoning: The tax channel standing alone had the highest Fama-MacBeth t-stat of any quality leg tested (2.57) but a weak alpha (+0.6%), the mirror image of the working-capital trend's profile, so combining them targets the study's exact weakness — jointly strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence. Paired with Signal 1 it identifies which third channel carries incremental information rather than just averaging noise.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BroadValueAmplifiedQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book-to-market is a noisy proxy for cheapness — it misprices asset-light and write-down-scarred firms — so a two-measure value composite (book and sales relative to price) should identify the firms where accounting quality matters more accurately than book-to-market alone.
evaluated.reasoning: The amplifier determines *where* the accrual interaction is switched on, and the archive shows it materially changes results (yield-based amplifiers turned the alpha negative, the hard gate destabilized the portfolio), so improving its measurement is a substantive change rather than a relabeling. Sales-to-price is available for firms with distorted book equity, which should also stabilize the extreme buckets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapWithQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Mispricing is best identified relative to a firm's *own* valuation history rather than the cross-section: a firm trading at the cheap end of its five-year book-to-market range while its accounting quality is improving has suffered a price decline unmatched by fundamentals.
evaluated.reasoning: A time-series cheapness amplifier is structurally orthogonal to HML — it contains no permanent industry or business-model value tilt, only firm-level valuation deviation — so it should isolate the accrual-quality interaction with even less factor contamination than cross-sectional B/M. This is the first valuation channel in the study measured in the time-series dimension, and it directly tests whether the interaction is about being cheap or about having become cheap.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithDeceleratingAccrualBuild
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The turning point matters more than the level or the slope: a cheap firm whose non-cash working capital intensity is still rising but decelerating is at the inflection where accrual pressure on future earnings peaks and begins to reverse, and the market prices the stale trend rather than the change in trend.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has tested accrual levels, one-year changes, five-year slopes, distance-from-peak and volatility, but never the second derivative, which is the earliest observable evidence that management is regaining working-capital discipline. It is a genuinely new temporal concept using the same well-covered balance-sheet inputs, so any result is attributable to the timing concept rather than to data availability.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithRevenueCashCollection
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(recch, 0), sale), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Revenue quality is the specific accrual channel behind the classic value trap: a cheap firm that persistently collects its sales in cash has real revenue, whereas one whose reported sales keep migrating into receivables is recognizing revenue it will not collect, so its cheapness reflects earnings that will be written down.
evaluated.reasoning: The receivables channel has only ever been tested in this study inside a gen-0 additive sales-yield composite whose dispersion came from the yield and whose FF5 alpha was therefore negative; measured as a three-year *state* and used as the dispersion leg under the HML-neutral amplifier, it is a new and economically sharp channel rather than a reweighting of an existing signal. Deflating by sales rather than assets ties the measure directly to revenue recognition, and averaging over three years removes the single-year collection-timing noise that killed one-year accrual legs earlier in the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapThreeChannel
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm trading cheap relative to its own valuation history is a genuine bargain only when its accounting is validated on three fronts — working-capital discipline, depreciation adequacy and taxes actually accrued — and the tax channel supplies the cross-sectional information the balance-sheet slopes lack.
evaluated.reasoning: The two best gen-4 findings were independent of each other — the time-series amplifier improved the portfolio evidence (alpha 3.9%, t 4.12) while the tax leg improved the cross-sectional evidence (fmb 3.87) — and no signal has yet combined them, so this directly targets the stated objective of joint strength rather than one metric. All three quality channels use densely populated annual items, so coverage should hold near the study norm of 0.10.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapNoAssetBloat
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual accumulation is not confined to working capital: a multi-year build-up of *total* net operating assets per dollar of sales — capitalized costs, acquired intangibles and unproductive plant as well as receivables and inventory — measures the full stock of unreversed accruals that will eventually be written down, so a dislocated-cheap firm shedding operating assets relative to sales is the credible bargain.
evaluated.reasoning: Every quality channel tested so far lives inside current assets and liabilities or in depreciation alone; net operating assets relative to sales spans both and captures capitalization decisions that working-capital measures miss entirely, making it the broadest untested accrual state in the resource menu. Pairing it with the study's best amplifier gives the new channel a fair test against the archive's incumbent.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FirmSpecificCheapAndCleanState
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Both cheapness and accounting quality are best judged against the firm's own history: a firm priced at the cheap end of its five-year range while its non-cash working-capital intensity sits at the lean end of its own five-year range is operationally tighter and cheaper than it has been, a combination the market systematically underprices.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the first construct in which *both* legs are purely time-series, so it carries no cross-sectional industry or business-model tilt at all and should be maximally orthogonal to the FF5 factors — the direction the evidence has been pointing since cross-sectional yields kept producing negative alphas. It also replaces a fitted five-year slope with a robust percentile-in-own-history measure, which is less sensitive to a single outlying fiscal year than TREND.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SalesAnchoredOwnHistoryCheapQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The valuation anchor used to identify dislocation should itself be free of accounting discretion: revenue is far harder to manipulate than book equity, so a firm priced cheaply against its own history of sales-to-price is dislocated for market reasons, and conditioning that dislocation on accrual quality isolates genuine mispricing.
evaluated.reasoning: Every amplifier tested so far uses book equity, which is contaminated by exactly the accrual and impairment decisions the quality leg is meant to police — a circularity that weakens the interaction, since write-downs mechanically move book-to-market. Replacing it with an own-history sales-to-price percentile keeps the time-series construction that carried all the portfolio evidence (alpha 3.9%, t 4.12) while removing accounting contamination from the valuation side, and unlike a cross-sectional sales yield it carries no permanent value tilt for HML to absorb.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConjunctiveQualityOwnHistoryCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5))), RANK(MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings credibility is a conjunction, not an average: a single unresolved red flag — either deteriorating cash conversion or book profits unaccompanied by accrued taxes — is enough to invalidate cheapness, so the binding weaker check should determine the quality score.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has only ever aggregated quality channels additively via SUMRANK, which lets a strong cash-conversion score mask an absent tax check; taking the minimum of the two percentiles encodes a genuinely different aggregation economics in which red flags cannot be averaged away. This also gives the MIN structure a fair test — previously it was applied across value and quality, where it merely mimicked the rank average and inherited the value tilt that produced negative alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapSalesOutpacingAssets
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1)), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The classic fundamental-analysis red flag is operating current assets growing faster than revenue: receivables and inventory outrunning sales means demand is being met with credit terms and unsold stock, so a dislocated-cheap firm whose sales growth persistently exceeds its operating-asset growth has real, collectible revenue.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the price-driven "freshly cheap" amplifier — which was really a disguised reversal bet — with a new *quality* channel measured as a growth differential rather than a deflated level or slope, the Lev-Thiagarajan diagnostic that the archive has never tested. Using non-cash current assets (act − che), a strictly positive quantity, keeps GROWTH well behaved, and the three-year average suppresses the single-year noise that killed every one-year accrual channel in the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithArticulatedAccounting
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(ib, oancf)), at)), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: When accruals computed from successive balance sheets disagree persistently with accruals implied by the cash-flow statement, the discrepancy reveals acquisitions, write-offs, reclassifications and restatements that make reported earnings unreliable; cheap firms whose two accounting systems articulate cleanly have trustworthy numbers.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a new economic channel — non-articulation as an audit-quality diagnostic — rather than another level, slope or dispersion of accruals, and it is measurable only because both measurement routes exist in the data. It differs from the failed ABS-accrual-opacity test in that it flags *inconsistency between two independent measurements* rather than the size of accruals themselves, so a firm with large but internally consistent accruals is not penalized.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OwnHistoryCheapRisingCashMargin
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness is validated not only by the absence of accrual build but by an improving *cash* margin after the depreciation charge that proxies the capital the business consumes; a dislocated-cheap firm whose post-depreciation cash margin has trended up for five years is earning more real cash per dollar of revenue than its price implies.
evaluated.reasoning: Every quality channel tested so far measures the *stock or slope of accruals* on the balance sheet; none measures accrual-free profitability dynamics, which is the economically prior question of whether the business is actually generating more cash per unit of sales. Subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow charges the firm for capital consumption, so the measure cannot be gamed by cutting maintenance capex the way a raw cash-margin trend can.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BothAnchorsCheapWithQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A price dislocation is credible only when the firm is cheap versus its own history on both an accounting anchor (book) and a real-activity anchor (sales); if only one anchor is depressed, the "cheapness" is an artifact of a write-down or a margin collapse rather than of price.
evaluated.reasoning: The previous version averaged the two anchors, which contradicted its own conjunctive claim; taking the minimum of the two own-history percentiles implements the hypothesis literally, so a firm whose book-to-market is at a five-year high only because equity was written down scores low. Both legs are densely populated and purely time-series, keeping the amplifier free of the cross-sectional value tilt that has repeatedly produced negative FF5 alphas here.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashFlowAnchoredDislocationQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The most theory-consistent way to identify a dislocated cheap firm in this study is against its own history of *cash-flow* yield, the one valuation anchor that management cannot manufacture with accruals, so cheapness on cash flow conditioned on a clean accrual state should be the purest version of cash-backed value.
evaluated.reasoning: The cross-sectional CFO/P amplifier failed badly (fmb 0.08, alpha −1.7%), but the archive later showed that failure is the signature of the cross-sectional value tilt rather than of the anchor, since the same book anchor flipped from −2.7% to +3.9% when moved into the time-series dimension. This is therefore a genuine economic test — is the anchor or the dimension responsible — rather than a lookback sweep, and it uses a valuation variable never tested in the winning architecture.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithConsistentCashBacking
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(TS_SUM(SIGN(SUB(SUB(oancf, ib), dp)), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What distinguishes a real bargain from a value trap is the *consistency* with which earnings have been converted to cash: counting how many of the last five years had a working-capital release rather than a build measures habitual accounting conservatism, immune to a single large distorting year.
evaluated.reasoning: Every quality leg in the archive is magnitude-based — a level, slope, cumulative sum, dispersion or peak distance — and magnitudes on annual accounting data are heavy-tailed, which is plausibly why several economically sound channels produced weak t-stats; a sign-count is a rank-robust reformulation of the same economics with entirely different noise properties. The algebra is exact: oancf − ib − dp is positive precisely when non-cash working capital fell, so the count rises with habitual cash backing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NoRedFlagQualityOwnHistoryCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The two accounting-quality dimensions that carry the archive's abnormal returns — working-capital discipline and depreciation adequacy — are complements rather than substitutes, so a cheap firm must clear both hurdles and a failure on either should not be offset by strength on the other.
evaluated.reasoning: The earlier conjunctive attempt died at 0% coverage because it took MIN across the sparsely reported txp leg, so this version conjoins the two densely populated channels that jointly produced the best alpha in the study when averaged (+3.9%, t 4.12), making the additive-versus-conjunctive comparison a clean, interpretable contrast on identical inputs. It differs from WeakestLinkCheapAndClean, which took MIN *across* valuation and quality and thereby inherited the cross-sectional value tilt that drove that signal's alpha negative.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CleanAndCashMarginHurdle
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness deserves trust only when the firm is both tightening its working capital and improving its post-depreciation cash margin; discipline without rising cash profitability is cost-cutting into decline, and rising cash margins with deteriorating working capital are unsustainable.
evaluated.reasoning: The cash-margin trend was the strongest new channel of gen 6 on cross-sectional evidence (fmb 2.98 with alpha 2.9%) and it measures accrual-free profitability dynamics rather than balance-sheet accrual states, making it the most economically complementary partner for the working-capital slope under a no-weak-link rule. It substitutes for the depreciation leg, whose standalone alpha t was only 1.46 and which the critic flagged as confounded by asset growth, so this is a channel upgrade rather than a reweighting.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConsistencyPlusDirectionCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(SIGN(SUB(SUB(oancf, ib), dp)), 5), NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Habitual cash backing (how many of the last five years released working capital) and the current direction of working-capital intensity are complementary facts about the same firm — one measures character, the other momentum — and a cheap firm needs both to be credible.
evaluated.reasoning: The sign-count leg produced a solid alpha (+3.2%, t 2.42) but an fmb of only 0.40 because an integer score taking six values is far too coarse for a cross-sectional level regression; pairing it with a continuous slope inside SUMRANK restores cross-sectional resolution while retaining the outlier-robust consistency information. This is a targeted repair of a diagnosed measurement defect rather than a new mechanism claim.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithWorkingCapitalBelowOwnNorm
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Each firm has a business-model-specific normal level of working capital per dollar of sales, so the informative accrual signal is the *deviation from that firm's own five-year norm* — currently operating leaner than usual means accruals are not being used to manufacture earnings, regardless of whether the level is high or low in the cross-section.
evaluated.reasoning: Every quality channel so far is either a cross-sectional comparison or a fitted slope; a deviation-from-own-mean measure is a different normalization that keeps magnitude information (unlike TS_RANK, whose five-point discreteness produced the lumpy fmb 1.78 result) while removing permanent industry and business-model differences that no cross-sectional rank can strip out here, since industry operators return zero coverage in this environment. It is dense, uses only well-populated balance-sheet items, and isolates the normalization choice against the trend incumbent.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PriceFellFundamentalsDidNot
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp)), sale)), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Mispricing is a *divergence*: the stock trades at the cheap end of its own five-year valuation range while its cash-based margin is not at the low end of its own five-year range, meaning the market has re-rated the equity without a matching deterioration in accrual-free profitability.
evaluated.reasoning: Every construct in the archive multiplies a cheapness weight by a quality score; this instead differences two own-history percentiles, so the signal is explicitly the *gap* between what the price says and what the cash-adjusted margin says, and firms whose cheapness is fully justified by collapsing cash margins are pushed to the middle rather than into the long leg. The margin is computed from balance-sheet accruals (ib less the working-capital accrual net of depreciation), which keeps coverage at the dense annual-fundamentals level rather than the thinner cash-flow-statement sample.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SelfFundedCleanCheapHurdles
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual-inflated earnings have to be financed: a firm whose reported cash conversion and depreciation look adequate but whose debt keeps rising relative to assets is not actually self-funding its operations, so financing self-sufficiency is a third, non-redundant hurdle a cheap firm must clear.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike the rejected net-operating-asset hurdle, which was arithmetically nested inside the working-capital leg it was meant to police, the financing leg comes from the right-hand side of the balance sheet and can veto a different set of firms — those whose operating metrics look clean precisely because creditors are funding the gap. This makes the conjunction span the cash cycle, cost recognition and funding, the three ways a value trap can sustain the appearance of quality.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookDislocationCleanCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The valuation anchor should be purged of soft assets before dislocation is measured: cheapness relative to a firm's own history of *hard* book value — equity excluding net non-cash working capital — cannot be manufactured by receivable and inventory accumulation, so it identifies price dislocation rather than accounting inflation.
evaluated.reasoning: Hard book-to-market was tested only as a cross-sectional ratio, where it behaved like every other yield (fmb 2.29, alpha −1.3%), and the archive's central finding is that moving a valuation anchor from the cross-section into the firm's own time series flips those negative alphas positive (book anchor: −2.7% cross-sectionally versus +3.9% in TS form). This is therefore a substantive test of an accrual-purged anchor in the dimension that works, not a repetition of the tax-veto structure whose coverage failure is now diagnosed as NaN propagation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BalanceSheetConsistencyPlusDirection
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(SIGN(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), 5), NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Habitual working-capital release — how many of the past five years the firm actually shrank its non-cash working capital — is the character trait that validates cheapness, and it can be observed from successive balance sheets without relying on cash-flow-statement detail.
evaluated.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement version of this construct produced the archive's highest alpha (+4.0%, t 3.38) but its coverage fell to 0.066, and every signal in this study with coverage under ~0.09 has shown unstable evidence, so re-deriving the same economic quantity from densely reported balance-sheet items is a targeted coverage repair rather than a new claim. If the alpha survives at ~0.10 coverage with a stronger fmb, the consistency channel becomes the study's leading quality leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookWithStableAccrualProcess
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Direction and stability of the accrual process are separate credibility dimensions: a dislocated-cheap firm whose working capital is both trending down and varying little year to year has a predictable, estimate-light accounting process, whereas an erratic accrual process signals discretionary management regardless of its trend.
evaluated.reasoning: Accrual volatility was tested once, under an earnings-yield amplifier that we now know contaminates any spread with HML exposure (alpha −1.7%), so the second-moment dimension has never had a fair test in the architecture that works. Pairing it additively with the trend under the purified anchor keeps coverage dense and asks whether stability adds information beyond direction — the one moment of the accrual distribution still unresolved.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookTaxVerifiedHalfWeight
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: External tax verification and internal cash conversion are the two independent credibility checks, and giving the tax check equal weight alongside working-capital discipline — under an anchor that cannot be inflated by accruals — should deliver cross-sectional and portfolio evidence simultaneously.
evaluated.reasoning: The tax channel has repeatedly moved the Fama-MacBeth slope (2.57 standalone; 3.87 inside a composite) but never received more than quarter weight in a composite that also had a strong anchor, and its only conjunctive test failed on NaN propagation, so equal additive weight with a dense partner leg is the untested configuration. Using the hard-book anchor addresses the archive's other regularity — that alpha lives in the purified own-history anchors — so this is aimed squarely at joint strength rather than at one metric.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: StandardizedDislocationCleanCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MA(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), VOL(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the *size* of the valuation dislocation relative to the firm's own normal variation: a book-to-market two standard deviations above its own five-year mean is a far stronger mispricing candidate than one merely at the top of a five-point rank, and stable-valuation firms need smaller absolute moves to be dislocated than volatile ones.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic has twice noted that a five-observation TS_RANK is coarse and lumpy, and this replaces it with a firm-specific standardized deviation that preserves magnitude and scales by the firm's own valuation volatility — a new economic claim (dislocation should be measured in units of the firm's own risk) rather than an operator swap between two archive signals. The outer cross-sectional RANK keeps the amplifier a strictly positive weight so the quality leg's sign is never flipped for expensive firms, which was the design feature that made the multiplicative architecture HML-neutral.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InvestedCapitalDislocationQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The dislocation that accounting quality should be conditioned on belongs to the *business*, not to the levered equity stub: comparing book invested capital (equity plus net debt) with the market value of that same invested capital measures how cheaply the whole enterprise trades relative to its own history, free of leverage amplification.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic correctly identified a numerator/denominator mismatch in the previous version — book equity over enterprise value mechanically penalizes levered firms — so this puts net invested capital in both numerator and denominator, which is the coherent capital-level analogue of book-to-market. Since leverage is the last known contaminant of the own-history anchor after the soft-asset purification worked (fmb 3.10, Sharpe 0.45), this tests whether de-levering the dislocation measure further sharpens the interaction while keeping dense balance-sheet coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HardBookChronicAccrualLevel
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Direction of working-capital intensity and the chronic *magnitude* of annual accruals are different facts: a firm can be tightening its ratio while still booking large accruals every year, so a dislocated-cheap firm is credible only when its average annual accrual per dollar of sales is small as well as falling.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the payout channel — which the critic rightly judged a payer dummy and weak evidence about earnings, since distributions can be debt-financed — with the accrual flow itself, averaged over five years so it measures habitual reliance rather than the single-year change that failed early in the archive. Both legs come from densely reported balance-sheet items under the purified hard-book anchor, so coverage should hold near 0.10 where the study's evidence has been reliable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapitalDislocationLevelAndTrend
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Credible cheapness requires accruals that are both small in habitual magnitude and falling in intensity; the chronic five-year average accrual per dollar of sales and the direction of working-capital intensity are separate facts, and neither the depreciation leg nor the trend alone captures the former.
evaluated.reasoning: The chronic-level channel produced alpha +3.2% (t 2.74, Sharpe 0.36) when paired with the hard-book anchor, and it avoids the asset-growth confound that the critic repeatedly flagged in the depreciation-intensity leg, so pairing it with the strongest anchor tests a quality composite that is entirely working-capital-based but spans magnitude and direction. It is the most economically pure statement of the value-trap mechanism the study has assembled.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapitalDislocationAccrualShareOfProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), ADD(ABS(ib), dp)), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The value-trap story is literally about the *share of reported profit that is accrual rather than cash*, so the right quality measure deflates accruals by the firm's earnings capacity rather than by sales or assets: a dislocated-cheap firm whose accruals consume a small fraction of its profit is reporting cash-backed income.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg in this study has been deflated by sales or assets, which measures accrual intensity of *activity*; deflating by earnings capacity measures accrual intensity of *reported profit*, which is the quantity the hypothesis is actually about and which reorders firms with high accruals but very high profits differently from firms with modest accruals and no profits. Using ABS(ib) plus depreciation in the denominator keeps the ratio finite for loss-makers and near-zero-earnings firms, the failure mode that makes naive accrual-to-earnings ratios explode.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OneSidedAccrualPenaltyCheap
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(MAX(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5), SUB(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5), TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The mechanism is one-sided: building working capital destroys the credibility of cheap earnings, but shrinking it faster and faster adds no further information once the firm is already releasing capital, so the penalty should apply only to the positive part of the accrual trend.
evaluated.reasoning: Every quality leg tested so far is linear in the accrual state, which implicitly assumes ever-greater working-capital contraction is ever-better news — economically doubtful, since aggressive liquidation is a distress symptom, not a quality signal. Truncating the trend at zero is a genuine functional-form claim about the mechanism rather than a new input, and pairing it with the depreciation leg inside SUMRANK breaks the tie mass created among all firms whose working capital is already falling.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingCapitalDislocationQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness should compare the book value of the *operating* capital a firm employs — assets excluding cash, net of non-debt operating liabilities — with the market value of exactly that operating capital, so the anchor measures how cheaply the market prices the productive asset base whose accounting quality the second leg audits.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic correctly showed the previous version's numerator collapsed to non-current assets while its denominator priced all operating assets, a base mismatch; defining the numerator as net operating assets and the denominator as enterprise value net of cash puts both sides on the same operating-capital base. This makes the anchor the direct book-to-market of the operating business, which is the object the accrual channels measure, rather than a mixture of equity, cash and leverage effects.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapitalDislocationHabitAcrossSystems
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(SIGN(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), 5), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting conservatism shows up as habit in the short-cycle accounts and as adequacy in the long-lived accounts: a de-levered dislocated firm that has repeatedly released working capital *and* charges depreciation at a rising rate is conservative in both accounting systems.
evaluated.reasoning: The previous version paired the sign count with the working-capital trend, two transformations of the same series, which the critic rightly judged mechanically redundant; replacing the partner leg with depreciation intensity puts the two legs in different parts of the balance sheet with genuinely different measurement errors. The count is also outlier-robust, which complements the slope leg's sensitivity to a single distorted fiscal year.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapitalDislocationTaxKeepingPaceWithSales
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), MA(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Real profits create real tax obligations: when accrued taxes keep growing in step with revenue, the reported income is being recognized by the tax authority as well as by management, whereas revenue growth unaccompanied by growing tax accruals is a signature of book-only earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: The tax channel has repeatedly moved the cross-sectional slope but only as a stale, size- and industry-confounded *level* (txp/at); expressing it as the change in accrued taxes per dollar of sales makes it a flow measure of tax verification that scales with the business, which is a different and better-specified variable rather than a reweighting. Paired at half weight with the working-capital slope under the study's best anchor, it targets the joint fmb-and-alpha objective with dense, well-populated inputs.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: CashEbitdaYieldBSAccrual
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: An operating-earnings yield built from EBITDA net of the balance-sheet working-capital accrual is a cleaner measure of distributable cash cheapness than any accounting-earnings yield.
considered.reasoning: Instead of ranking two separate channels, this embeds the Sloan-style balance-sheet accrual directly inside the numerator of the valuation ratio, so a firm looks cheap only if its operating profit is not financed by receivable/inventory build-ups. The balance-sheet accrual construction is independent of cash-flow-statement reporting conventions, giving a different measurement path than signals 1-3.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SalesYieldReceivableBacked
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(recch, 0), COALESCE(invch, 0)), at))
considered.hypothesis: Sales-based cheapness is trustworthy only when revenue is converted into cash rather than parked in receivables and inventory.
considered.reasoning: Sales-to-price avoids earnings management in the denominator of profitability but is vulnerable to channel-stuffing; recch and invch (cash-flow-statement decreases in receivables/inventory, positive when working capital releases cash) test exactly that conversion. COALESCE to zero is justified because an unreported working-capital line item means no disclosed change, not a missing firm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EarningsYieldPerAccrualNoise
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: High earnings yield is only informative when the accrual wedge is stable; volatile accruals signal unreliable, mean-reverting earnings that make apparent cheapness illusory.
considered.reasoning: This uses accrual *instability* rather than accrual level as the quality dimension, so it captures a second-moment interaction: cheap firms with a persistently small earnings-cash gap are credible, while cheap firms whose accrual gap swings across years are likely managing or misstating earnings. It is mechanically distinct from level-based accrual screens and should separate stable value from opaque value.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ValueWithWorkingCapitalDiscipline
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Cheap firms are rewarded when revenue is being generated with shrinking (not expanding) non-cash working capital, because a rising working-capital intensity of sales is the balance-sheet footprint of soft revenue recognition and predicts earnings reversal.
considered.reasoning: The valuation channel (book-to-market) and the accrual channel (change in non-cash working capital per dollar of sales) share no variable, so the composite genuinely combines two independent sources of information rather than re-deriving CFO/P from oancf twice. Scaling working capital by sales rather than assets makes the accrual leg a revenue-quality measure, distinguishing operationally lean cheap firms from cheap firms whose reported growth is trapped in receivables and inventory.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapnessPerAccrualOpacity
considered.expression: RATIO(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ADD(RANK(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), 1))
considered.hypothesis: What kills the value premium is not the sign of accruals but the magnitude of the accrual wedge: large absolute accruals — in either direction — signal low earnings reliability, so cheapness should be discounted hyperbolically by accounting opacity.
considered.reasoning: Using ABS of the accrual wedge makes the quality dimension an information-risk (accrual-quality) measure that is not monotone in signed accruals, so this is not a rotation of the signed rank sum in proposal 1. The divisive form imposes strong convex penalization: opaque firms are pushed toward zero regardless of how cheap they look, while transparent cheap firms retain their full valuation score, which is exactly the asymmetry a rank sum cannot represent.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardBookToMarketNetAccruals
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, TS_SUM(SUB(ib, oancf), 3)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: Accruals accumulate inside book equity, so a portion of reported book value is soft accounting rather than realized cash; the "hard" book value obtained by removing the last three years of accrual accumulation is the cheapness measure that should predict returns.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the degenerate zero-gate with a continuous adjustment inside the valuation ratio itself, so there is no mass point and no short leg that ignores valuation — the cross-section stays smooth and quantile breakpoints remain stable. Cumulating the wedge over three years captures the stock (not the flow) of accrual-inflated equity, distinguishing firms whose book value reflects retained cash from those whose book value reflects unreversed accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWeightedAccrualQuality
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Among cheap firms, the return spread is driven by whether reported profits are backed by cash rather than by working-capital build-up; cheapness itself should act as an amplifier of the accrual effect, not as the sorting variable.
considered.reasoning: The centered accrual-quality rank supplies the cross-sectional dispersion while RANK(book-to-market) only scales its magnitude, so the long and short legs hold comparably cheap firms and the spread is close to HML-neutral — exactly the flaw that made gen-0 FF5 alphas negative. Economically it implements the value-trap story literally: long cheap-and-cash-backed, short cheap-and-accrual-financed, with glamour firms parked near zero.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithConservativeDepreciation
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness is trustworthy when the firm charges heavy depreciation relative to its asset base for its industry, because aggressive capitalization and stretched useful lives inflate book earnings and book equity, producing artificial cheapness.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the working-capital accrual channel with a long-lived-asset accrual channel (depreciation adequacy), which is the second and largely independent component of total accruals, and industry-ranking removes the capital-intensity confound that would otherwise make dp/at an industry bet. Like Signal 1 it keeps both legs equally cheap, so any alpha should be residual to HML rather than a repackaged value premium.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithFallingWorkingCapitalTrend
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year upward drift in working capital per dollar of sales reveals a slow, persistent accrual build that one-year accrual measures miss; cheap firms with such a drift are value traps, while cheap firms tightening working capital are genuine bargains.
considered.reasoning: The economic content is a state variable (chronic deterioration of operating discipline) rather than a single-year flow, which should be less noisy and less mechanically reversing than DELTA-based accruals, so it isolates whether persistence or timing carries the information. It shares the conditioning architecture of Signal 1 deliberately, so the comparison cleanly identifies the value of the temporal dimension.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashEbitdaToEnterpriseValue
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ebitda, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-converted operating profit should be priced against the whole capital structure; the accrual-adjusted operating yield is informative about mispricing only once the leverage tilt in an equity-only deflator is removed.
considered.reasoning: This directly addresses the critic's objection to the gen-0 winner: an unlevered numerator over levered equity value created a leverage bet that plausibly contributed to the negative FF5 alpha, since leverage correlates with HML and CMA loadings. Keeping everything else identical makes the enterprise-value deflator a clean, single-design-choice test of whether the negative alpha was a leverage artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithLowAccrualOpacity
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))))
considered.hypothesis: For cheap stocks it is the *magnitude* of the non-cash working-capital swing, in either direction, that signals unreliable accounting; large absolute accruals mean the reported number is an estimate rather than a realization, so cheapness is only credible when the accrual footprint is small.
considered.reasoning: Dropping depreciation from the numerator removes the capital-intensity dominance the critic identified, and taking ABS makes this an accounting-opacity (information-risk) channel that is non-monotone in signed accruals, so it is not the published price-scaled accrual measure nor a restatement of the accepted signed-accrual signals. Keeping cheapness as a multiplicative weight on a centered rank means both legs hold comparably cheap firms, so any alpha is residual to HML rather than a repackaged value premium.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ValueRankMigrationOnCashEarnings
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
considered.hypothesis: What matters is whether a firm still looks cheap after its earnings are restated onto a cash basis: firms that climb the earnings-yield ranking under the accrual adjustment are genuinely cheap, while firms that fall down the ranking only appeared cheap because accruals inflated reported income.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the additive two-anomaly stack with a within-firm comparison of two valuation percentiles, so the level of cheapness differences out and the surviving variation is purely the accrual content of the earnings the market is capitalizing — an explicit interaction rather than a sum of separate effects. Measuring the shift in percentile units (not in accrual dollars per share price) normalizes for local density of the value distribution, avoids the dividend-payer tie mass, and keeps coverage as broad as the standard earnings-yield sample.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapFallingNoncashWCTrend
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year rise in *non-cash* working capital per dollar of sales is the signature of a chronic accrual build; cheap firms with that drift are value traps, while cheap firms whose non-cash working capital is shrinking relative to sales have cash-validated cheapness.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the one clear portfolio winner by removing cash and short-term debt from the accrual leg, so a cheap firm accumulating cash is no longer mislabeled as accrual-financed — the exact contradiction the critic identified. Everything else (conditional architecture, 5-year trend, cheapness weight) is held fixed, making this a clean test of whether cleaning the accrual definition strengthens both the FMB slope and the alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithRisingDepreciationIntensity
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The long-lived-asset accrual channel works through depreciation adequacy: firms that let depreciation intensity drift down are stretching useful lives and capitalizing costs to prop up book earnings, so their cheapness is manufactured, whereas cheap firms with rising depreciation intensity are recognizing costs conservatively.
considered.reasoning: It resurrects the depreciation channel that scored highest with the critic but died at 0% coverage because industry operators are unavailable in this environment; using a within-firm 5-year trend instead of IND_RANK removes the capital-intensity confound through the firm's own history rather than through peers. This is the only proposal that sources accrual quality outside working capital, so it diversifies the archive's dominant channel.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapCashFlowNotPayableFunded
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(apalch, 0), COALESCE(txach, 0)), at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Even cash-flow-based cheapness can be fake: operating cash flow inflated by stretching payables and deferring tax remittances is borrowed liquidity, not earned cash, so cheap-on-CFO firms whose CFO is funded by payable and tax accruals underperform.
considered.reasoning: This attacks the one construct the critic said subsumes both themes (CFO/P) by decomposing the *source* of the cash flow, which no archive signal does — the quality leg uses only liability-side cash-flow-statement accruals and is therefore mechanically independent of the receivable/inventory and depreciation channels already tested. COALESCE-to-zero is defensible because an unreported payables or tax-accrual line means no disclosed change in that item.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EarningsYieldWithStableAccruals
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: High earnings yield is informative only when the accrual process is stable; erratic year-to-year swings in non-cash working capital intensity indicate estimate-driven, non-persistent earnings, so apparent cheapness on those earnings is unreliable.
considered.reasoning: This restores the second-moment idea that the validator rejected earlier for lacking an accruals-exclusive variable, now built from act/lct so it qualifies and is measured on the balance sheet. It is the only proposal keyed to accrual *instability* rather than accrual level or slope, and it pairs with an earnings-yield rather than book-based valuation weight, so it teaches a different lesson than Signals 1-3.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WeakestLinkCheapAndClean
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness and accounting quality are complements with no substitutability: a firm must clear both hurdles to be a genuine bargain, and failing either one is sufficient to disqualify it, so the binding constraint — the weaker of the two percentile scores — should price the stock.
considered.reasoning: The MIN operator encodes a conjunctive (Leontief) interaction that is neither a rank sum, a rank product, nor a gate, so the long leg is cheap-and-clean while the short leg contains firms that fail on either dimension — a structurally different portfolio composition from every archive signal. Testing it tells us whether the value-trap mechanism is better described as a joint hurdle than as a continuous weighting, using the accrual channel that has already shown portfolio-level promise.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapAfterAccrualUnwind
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual bloat must eventually reverse through the income statement, so the attractive moment to own a cheap stock is *after* the unwind: firms whose non-cash working capital intensity now sits far below its own five-year peak have already absorbed the earnings hit, leaving depressed reported earnings, a low price, and cash-backed forward earnings.
considered.reasoning: This is a genuine new signal rather than a monotone re-scaling: distance-from-own-maximum measures the *state of completion* of the accrual reversal, which is economically and mechanically distinct from a five-year slope (Signal 1), a dispersion measure (Signal 4), or a one-year flow, and it changes the sorted portfolios. It also sharpens the value-trap story into a timing statement — cheapness is safest once the accrual overhang has been worked off — while keeping the HML-neutral conditional architecture that produced the archive's only positive FF5 alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapTwoChannelAccrualState
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Working-capital discipline and depreciation adequacy are two largely independent dimensions of accounting quality, so a cheap firm that scores well on both has genuinely cash-validated cheapness and the combined quality state should predict returns more reliably than either channel alone.
considered.reasoning: Both ingredient channels delivered positive but individually imprecise FF5 alphas (t = 2.70 and 1.46) from different parts of the accounting system — current operating assets versus long-lived assets — so averaging their ranks should cancel channel-specific noise and raise both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha rather than just relabel one of them. This is the batch's consolidation move, using the archive as evidence about which channels to combine.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithCumulativeCashConversion
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(SUB(oancf, ib), dp), 5), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Accounting quality is a multi-year property: a cheap firm whose cumulative five-year working-capital accrual (earnings minus cash flow, net of depreciation) is negative has been converting profit into cash for years, whereas a persistent positive cumulative accrual marks earnings that have been borrowed from the future.
considered.reasoning: This measures the same "state not flow" insight that made the trend channels work, but via cumulative cash-flow-statement conversion rather than a balance-sheet slope, and removing depreciation prevents the capital-intensity confound the critic raised about dp/at. It is the cleanest available test of whether the persistence of cash backing — rather than its direction of change — is what supports cheapness.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DeepValueOnlyAccrualState
considered.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The value-trap mechanism is nonlinear in cheapness: accounting quality matters decisively only where the market is pricing the equity below book value, because that is where the market is implicitly betting the reported earnings will not persist.
