considered.reasoning: A continuous rank amplifier spreads the interaction over the whole cross-section, whereas the hard price-to-book cutoff concentrates both legs inside the deep-value subsample where the economics bite, and the discarded firms sit at zero in the *middle* of the distribution rather than at an extreme, so breakpoints stay interpretable. It tests convexity of the amplifier, a design dimension the archive has never probed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithTaxVerifiedEarnings
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Income taxes payable are a third-party-verified claim that arises only when profits are real in the tax authority's eyes, so a cheap firm that persistently carries meaningful accrued taxes has earnings validated outside the accounting discretion of management, while a cheap firm reporting book profits with negligible tax liabilities is likely reporting accrual-inflated income.
considered.reasoning: This opens the tax channel, which is untouched in the archive and is economically independent of both working-capital slopes and depreciation adequacy — book-tax divergence is the classic external check on earnings quality. The three-year average implements the archive's clearest lesson (multi-year states beat one-year flows) while txp is a densely populated balance-sheet item, so coverage should match the study's norm rather than shrink like the cash-flow-statement lines.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapNotSupplierFinanced
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Conventional accrual measures treat rising operating liabilities as good news (a negative accrual), but for cheap firms a multi-year build-up of non-debt current liabilities per dollar of sales is supplier and tax financing of a strained business, and such firms underperform despite looking cash-generative.
considered.reasoning: This isolates the *liability side* of the accrual identity — the component that the asset-side channels (receivables, inventory, depreciation) already tested cannot speak to — and it deliberately reverses the sign convention that Sloan-style measures impose, making it a falsifiable economic claim rather than a patch. Unlike the abandoned apalch/txach version it uses densely reported balance-sheet items and changes exactly one thing relative to the archive's trend architecture, so the result is attributable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardAssetBookToMarket
considered.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
considered.hypothesis: Book equity is a mixture of hard components (cash, long-lived assets) and soft, estimate-laden net working capital (receivables and inventories net of operating liabilities); cheapness backed by hard book value is real, while cheapness backed mostly by soft working capital is an accounting artifact that reverses.
considered.reasoning: Unlike a three-year accrual haircut, non-cash working capital is typically a large fraction of book equity — often tens of percent, and negative for cash-rich firms — so this construct reorders the value cross-section substantially rather than replicating HML's ranking. It gives the study one non-conditional test whose economic content is the *composition* of book value rather than its level, which is the mechanism by which HML mistakes soft-asset firms for bargains.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ThreeChannelQualityCheap
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5), RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))))
considered.hypothesis: Accounting quality supporting cheapness has three separable dimensions — working-capital discipline, depreciation adequacy, and the completed unwinding of past accrual bloat — and a cheap firm scoring well on all three has earnings that are simultaneously cash-converted, conservatively costed, and free of an unreversed overhang.
considered.reasoning: Two-channel averaging raised the FF5 alpha from 2.2% to 3.0% and the t-stat from 2.70 to 3.42, so the natural test is whether the third channel that also produced standalone positive alpha (accrual unwind, +1.6%, t 1.85) adds further independent information or is redundant with the working-capital slope. The three legs use different accounting objects (level slope, long-lived-asset charge, distance from own historical peak), so their errors should be weakly correlated.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: QualityCompositeWithTaxCheck
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: External verification by the tax authority is a distinct form of earnings validation from internal cash conversion, so adding persistent accrued taxes to the quality composite should identify cheap firms whose profits are real to both the cash cycle and the taxman.
considered.reasoning: The tax channel standing alone had the highest Fama-MacBeth t-stat of any quality leg tested (2.57) but a weak alpha (+0.6%), the mirror image of the working-capital trend's profile, so combining them targets the study's exact weakness — jointly strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence. Paired with Signal 1 it identifies which third channel carries incremental information rather than just averaging noise.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BroadValueAmplifiedQuality
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Book-to-market is a noisy proxy for cheapness — it misprices asset-light and write-down-scarred firms — so a two-measure value composite (book and sales relative to price) should identify the firms where accounting quality matters more accurately than book-to-market alone.
considered.reasoning: The amplifier determines *where* the accrual interaction is switched on, and the archive shows it materially changes results (yield-based amplifiers turned the alpha negative, the hard gate destabilized the portfolio), so improving its measurement is a substantive change rather than a relabeling. Sales-to-price is available for firms with distorted book equity, which should also stabilize the extreme buckets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OwnHistoryCheapWithQuality
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Mispricing is best identified relative to a firm's *own* valuation history rather than the cross-section: a firm trading at the cheap end of its five-year book-to-market range while its accounting quality is improving has suffered a price decline unmatched by fundamentals.
considered.reasoning: A time-series cheapness amplifier is structurally orthogonal to HML — it contains no permanent industry or business-model value tilt, only firm-level valuation deviation — so it should isolate the accrual-quality interaction with even less factor contamination than cross-sectional B/M. This is the first valuation channel in the study measured in the time-series dimension, and it directly tests whether the interaction is about being cheap or about having become cheap.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithDeceleratingAccrualBuild
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale))))))
considered.hypothesis: The turning point matters more than the level or the slope: a cheap firm whose non-cash working capital intensity is still rising but decelerating is at the inflection where accrual pressure on future earnings peaks and begins to reverse, and the market prices the stale trend rather than the change in trend.
considered.reasoning: The archive has tested accrual levels, one-year changes, five-year slopes, distance-from-peak and volatility, but never the second derivative, which is the earliest observable evidence that management is regaining working-capital discipline. It is a genuinely new temporal concept using the same well-covered balance-sheet inputs, so any result is attributable to the timing concept rather than to data availability.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithRevenueCashCollection
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(recch, 0), sale), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Revenue quality is the specific accrual channel behind the classic value trap: a cheap firm that persistently collects its sales in cash has real revenue, whereas one whose reported sales keep migrating into receivables is recognizing revenue it will not collect, so its cheapness reflects earnings that will be written down.
considered.reasoning: The receivables channel has only ever been tested in this study inside a gen-0 additive sales-yield composite whose dispersion came from the yield and whose FF5 alpha was therefore negative; measured as a three-year *state* and used as the dispersion leg under the HML-neutral amplifier, it is a new and economically sharp channel rather than a reweighting of an existing signal. Deflating by sales rather than assets ties the measure directly to revenue recognition, and averaging over three years removes the single-year collection-timing noise that killed one-year accrual legs earlier in the archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OwnHistoryCheapThreeChannel
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm trading cheap relative to its own valuation history is a genuine bargain only when its accounting is validated on three fronts — working-capital discipline, depreciation adequacy and taxes actually accrued — and the tax channel supplies the cross-sectional information the balance-sheet slopes lack.
considered.reasoning: The two best gen-4 findings were independent of each other — the time-series amplifier improved the portfolio evidence (alpha 3.9%, t 4.12) while the tax leg improved the cross-sectional evidence (fmb 3.87) — and no signal has yet combined them, so this directly targets the stated objective of joint strength rather than one metric. All three quality channels use densely populated annual items, so coverage should hold near the study norm of 0.10.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OwnHistoryCheapNoAssetBloat
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual accumulation is not confined to working capital: a multi-year build-up of *total* net operating assets per dollar of sales — capitalized costs, acquired intangibles and unproductive plant as well as receivables and inventory — measures the full stock of unreversed accruals that will eventually be written down, so a dislocated-cheap firm shedding operating assets relative to sales is the credible bargain.
considered.reasoning: Every quality channel tested so far lives inside current assets and liabilities or in depreciation alone; net operating assets relative to sales spans both and captures capitalization decisions that working-capital measures miss entirely, making it the broadest untested accrual state in the resource menu. Pairing it with the study's best amplifier gives the new channel a fair test against the archive's incumbent.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FirmSpecificCheapAndCleanState
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale)), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Both cheapness and accounting quality are best judged against the firm's own history: a firm priced at the cheap end of its five-year range while its non-cash working-capital intensity sits at the lean end of its own five-year range is operationally tighter and cheaper than it has been, a combination the market systematically underprices.
considered.reasoning: This is the first construct in which *both* legs are purely time-series, so it carries no cross-sectional industry or business-model tilt at all and should be maximally orthogonal to the FF5 factors — the direction the evidence has been pointing since cross-sectional yields kept producing negative alphas. It also replaces a fitted five-year slope with a robust percentile-in-own-history measure, which is less sensitive to a single outlying fiscal year than TREND.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SalesAnchoredOwnHistoryCheapQuality
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The valuation anchor used to identify dislocation should itself be free of accounting discretion: revenue is far harder to manipulate than book equity, so a firm priced cheaply against its own history of sales-to-price is dislocated for market reasons, and conditioning that dislocation on accrual quality isolates genuine mispricing.
considered.reasoning: Every amplifier tested so far uses book equity, which is contaminated by exactly the accrual and impairment decisions the quality leg is meant to police — a circularity that weakens the interaction, since write-downs mechanically move book-to-market. Replacing it with an own-history sales-to-price percentile keeps the time-series construction that carried all the portfolio evidence (alpha 3.9%, t 4.12) while removing accounting contamination from the valuation side, and unlike a cross-sectional sales yield it carries no permanent value tilt for HML to absorb.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConjunctiveQualityOwnHistoryCheap
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5))), RANK(MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings credibility is a conjunction, not an average: a single unresolved red flag — either deteriorating cash conversion or book profits unaccompanied by accrued taxes — is enough to invalidate cheapness, so the binding weaker check should determine the quality score.
considered.reasoning: The archive has only ever aggregated quality channels additively via SUMRANK, which lets a strong cash-conversion score mask an absent tax check; taking the minimum of the two percentiles encodes a genuinely different aggregation economics in which red flags cannot be averaged away. This also gives the MIN structure a fair test — previously it was applied across value and quality, where it merely mimicked the rank average and inherited the value tilt that produced negative alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OwnHistoryCheapSalesOutpacingAssets
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(MA(SUB(GROWTH(sale, 1), GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1)), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: The classic fundamental-analysis red flag is operating current assets growing faster than revenue: receivables and inventory outrunning sales means demand is being met with credit terms and unsold stock, so a dislocated-cheap firm whose sales growth persistently exceeds its operating-asset growth has real, collectible revenue.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the price-driven "freshly cheap" amplifier — which was really a disguised reversal bet — with a new *quality* channel measured as a growth differential rather than a deflated level or slope, the Lev-Thiagarajan diagnostic that the archive has never tested. Using non-cash current assets (act − che), a strictly positive quantity, keeps GROWTH well behaved, and the three-year average suppresses the single-year noise that killed every one-year accrual channel in the archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithArticulatedAccounting
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), SUB(ib, oancf)), at)), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: When accruals computed from successive balance sheets disagree persistently with accruals implied by the cash-flow statement, the discrepancy reveals acquisitions, write-offs, reclassifications and restatements that make reported earnings unreliable; cheap firms whose two accounting systems articulate cleanly have trustworthy numbers.
considered.reasoning: This is a new economic channel — non-articulation as an audit-quality diagnostic — rather than another level, slope or dispersion of accruals, and it is measurable only because both measurement routes exist in the data. It differs from the failed ABS-accrual-opacity test in that it flags *inconsistency between two independent measurements* rather than the size of accruals themselves, so a firm with large but internally consistent accruals is not penalized.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OwnHistoryCheapRisingCashMargin
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), sale), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness is validated not only by the absence of accrual build but by an improving *cash* margin after the depreciation charge that proxies the capital the business consumes; a dislocated-cheap firm whose post-depreciation cash margin has trended up for five years is earning more real cash per dollar of revenue than its price implies.
considered.reasoning: Every quality channel tested so far measures the *stock or slope of accruals* on the balance sheet; none measures accrual-free profitability dynamics, which is the economically prior question of whether the business is actually generating more cash per unit of sales. Subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow charges the firm for capital consumption, so the measure cannot be gamed by cutting maintenance capex the way a raw cash-margin trend can.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BothAnchorsCheapWithQuality
considered.expression: MUL(MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: A price dislocation is credible only when the firm is cheap versus its own history on both an accounting anchor (book) and a real-activity anchor (sales); if only one anchor is depressed, the "cheapness" is an artifact of a write-down or a margin collapse rather than of price.
considered.reasoning: The previous version averaged the two anchors, which contradicted its own conjunctive claim; taking the minimum of the two own-history percentiles implements the hypothesis literally, so a firm whose book-to-market is at a five-year high only because equity was written down scores low. Both legs are densely populated and purely time-series, keeping the amplifier free of the cross-sectional value tilt that has repeatedly produced negative FF5 alphas here.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashFlowAnchoredDislocationQuality
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The most theory-consistent way to identify a dislocated cheap firm in this study is against its own history of *cash-flow* yield, the one valuation anchor that management cannot manufacture with accruals, so cheapness on cash flow conditioned on a clean accrual state should be the purest version of cash-backed value.
considered.reasoning: The cross-sectional CFO/P amplifier failed badly (fmb 0.08, alpha −1.7%), but the archive later showed that failure is the signature of the cross-sectional value tilt rather than of the anchor, since the same book anchor flipped from −2.7% to +3.9% when moved into the time-series dimension. This is therefore a genuine economic test — is the anchor or the dimension responsible — rather than a lookback sweep, and it uses a valuation variable never tested in the winning architecture.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithConsistentCashBacking
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(TS_SUM(SIGN(SUB(SUB(oancf, ib), dp)), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: What distinguishes a real bargain from a value trap is the *consistency* with which earnings have been converted to cash: counting how many of the last five years had a working-capital release rather than a build measures habitual accounting conservatism, immune to a single large distorting year.
considered.reasoning: Every quality leg in the archive is magnitude-based — a level, slope, cumulative sum, dispersion or peak distance — and magnitudes on annual accounting data are heavy-tailed, which is plausibly why several economically sound channels produced weak t-stats; a sign-count is a rank-robust reformulation of the same economics with entirely different noise properties. The algebra is exact: oancf − ib − dp is positive precisely when non-cash working capital fell, so the count rises with habitual cash backing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NoRedFlagQualityOwnHistoryCheap
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The two accounting-quality dimensions that carry the archive's abnormal returns — working-capital discipline and depreciation adequacy — are complements rather than substitutes, so a cheap firm must clear both hurdles and a failure on either should not be offset by strength on the other.
considered.reasoning: The earlier conjunctive attempt died at 0% coverage because it took MIN across the sparsely reported txp leg, so this version conjoins the two densely populated channels that jointly produced the best alpha in the study when averaged (+3.9%, t 4.12), making the additive-versus-conjunctive comparison a clean, interpretable contrast on identical inputs. It differs from WeakestLinkCheapAndClean, which took MIN *across* valuation and quality and thereby inherited the cross-sectional value tilt that drove that signal's alpha negative.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CleanAndCashMarginHurdle
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness deserves trust only when the firm is both tightening its working capital and improving its post-depreciation cash margin; discipline without rising cash profitability is cost-cutting into decline, and rising cash margins with deteriorating working capital are unsustainable.
considered.reasoning: The cash-margin trend was the strongest new channel of gen 6 on cross-sectional evidence (fmb 2.98 with alpha 2.9%) and it measures accrual-free profitability dynamics rather than balance-sheet accrual states, making it the most economically complementary partner for the working-capital slope under a no-weak-link rule. It substitutes for the depreciation leg, whose standalone alpha t was only 1.46 and which the critic flagged as confounded by asset growth, so this is a channel upgrade rather than a reweighting.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConsistencyPlusDirectionCheap
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(SIGN(SUB(SUB(oancf, ib), dp)), 5), NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Habitual cash backing (how many of the last five years released working capital) and the current direction of working-capital intensity are complementary facts about the same firm — one measures character, the other momentum — and a cheap firm needs both to be credible.
considered.reasoning: The sign-count leg produced a solid alpha (+3.2%, t 2.42) but an fmb of only 0.40 because an integer score taking six values is far too coarse for a cross-sectional level regression; pairing it with a continuous slope inside SUMRANK restores cross-sectional resolution while retaining the outlier-robust consistency information. This is a targeted repair of a diagnosed measurement defect rather than a new mechanism claim.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CheapWithWorkingCapitalBelowOwnNorm
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))))))
considered.hypothesis: Each firm has a business-model-specific normal level of working capital per dollar of sales, so the informative accrual signal is the *deviation from that firm's own five-year norm* — currently operating leaner than usual means accruals are not being used to manufacture earnings, regardless of whether the level is high or low in the cross-section.
considered.reasoning: Every quality channel so far is either a cross-sectional comparison or a fitted slope; a deviation-from-own-mean measure is a different normalization that keeps magnitude information (unlike TS_RANK, whose five-point discreteness produced the lumpy fmb 1.78 result) while removing permanent industry and business-model differences that no cross-sectional rank can strip out here, since industry operators return zero coverage in this environment. It is dense, uses only well-populated balance-sheet items, and isolates the normalization choice against the trend incumbent.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PriceFellFundamentalsDidNot
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp)), sale)), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Mispricing is a *divergence*: the stock trades at the cheap end of its own five-year valuation range while its cash-based margin is not at the low end of its own five-year range, meaning the market has re-rated the equity without a matching deterioration in accrual-free profitability.
considered.reasoning: Every construct in the archive multiplies a cheapness weight by a quality score; this instead differences two own-history percentiles, so the signal is explicitly the *gap* between what the price says and what the cash-adjusted margin says, and firms whose cheapness is fully justified by collapsing cash margins are pushed to the middle rather than into the long leg. The margin is computed from balance-sheet accruals (ib less the working-capital accrual net of depreciation), which keeps coverage at the dense annual-fundamentals level rather than the thinner cash-flow-statement sample.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SelfFundedCleanCheapHurdles
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual-inflated earnings have to be financed: a firm whose reported cash conversion and depreciation look adequate but whose debt keeps rising relative to assets is not actually self-funding its operations, so financing self-sufficiency is a third, non-redundant hurdle a cheap firm must clear.
considered.reasoning: Unlike the rejected net-operating-asset hurdle, which was arithmetically nested inside the working-capital leg it was meant to police, the financing leg comes from the right-hand side of the balance sheet and can veto a different set of firms — those whose operating metrics look clean precisely because creditors are funding the gap. This makes the conjunction span the cash cycle, cost recognition and funding, the three ways a value trap can sustain the appearance of quality.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardBookDislocationCleanCheap
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), MIN(ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), ZSCORE(RANK(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The valuation anchor should be purged of soft assets before dislocation is measured: cheapness relative to a firm's own history of *hard* book value — equity excluding net non-cash working capital — cannot be manufactured by receivable and inventory accumulation, so it identifies price dislocation rather than accounting inflation.
considered.reasoning: Hard book-to-market was tested only as a cross-sectional ratio, where it behaved like every other yield (fmb 2.29, alpha −1.3%), and the archive's central finding is that moving a valuation anchor from the cross-section into the firm's own time series flips those negative alphas positive (book anchor: −2.7% cross-sectionally versus +3.9% in TS form). This is therefore a substantive test of an accrual-purged anchor in the dimension that works, not a repetition of the tax-veto structure whose coverage failure is now diagnosed as NaN propagation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BalanceSheetConsistencyPlusDirection
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(SIGN(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), 5), NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Habitual working-capital release — how many of the past five years the firm actually shrank its non-cash working capital — is the character trait that validates cheapness, and it can be observed from successive balance sheets without relying on cash-flow-statement detail.
considered.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement version of this construct produced the archive's highest alpha (+4.0%, t 3.38) but its coverage fell to 0.066, and every signal in this study with coverage under ~0.09 has shown unstable evidence, so re-deriving the same economic quantity from densely reported balance-sheet items is a targeted coverage repair rather than a new claim. If the alpha survives at ~0.10 coverage with a stronger fmb, the consistency channel becomes the study's leading quality leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardBookWithStableAccrualProcess
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Direction and stability of the accrual process are separate credibility dimensions: a dislocated-cheap firm whose working capital is both trending down and varying little year to year has a predictable, estimate-light accounting process, whereas an erratic accrual process signals discretionary management regardless of its trend.
considered.reasoning: Accrual volatility was tested once, under an earnings-yield amplifier that we now know contaminates any spread with HML exposure (alpha −1.7%), so the second-moment dimension has never had a fair test in the architecture that works. Pairing it additively with the trend under the purified anchor keeps coverage dense and asks whether stability adds information beyond direction — the one moment of the accrual distribution still unresolved.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardBookTaxVerifiedHalfWeight
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), MA(RATIO(txp, at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: External tax verification and internal cash conversion are the two independent credibility checks, and giving the tax check equal weight alongside working-capital discipline — under an anchor that cannot be inflated by accruals — should deliver cross-sectional and portfolio evidence simultaneously.
considered.reasoning: The tax channel has repeatedly moved the Fama-MacBeth slope (2.57 standalone; 3.87 inside a composite) but never received more than quarter weight in a composite that also had a strong anchor, and its only conjunctive test failed on NaN propagation, so equal additive weight with a dense partner leg is the untested configuration. Using the hard-book anchor addresses the archive's other regularity — that alpha lives in the purified own-history anchors — so this is aimed squarely at joint strength rather than at one metric.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StandardizedDislocationCleanCheap
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MA(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), VOL(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5))), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: What matters is the *size* of the valuation dislocation relative to the firm's own normal variation: a book-to-market two standard deviations above its own five-year mean is a far stronger mispricing candidate than one merely at the top of a five-point rank, and stable-valuation firms need smaller absolute moves to be dislocated than volatile ones.
considered.reasoning: The critic has twice noted that a five-observation TS_RANK is coarse and lumpy, and this replaces it with a firm-specific standardized deviation that preserves magnitude and scales by the firm's own valuation volatility — a new economic claim (dislocation should be measured in units of the firm's own risk) rather than an operator swap between two archive signals. The outer cross-sectional RANK keeps the amplifier a strictly positive weight so the quality leg's sign is never flipped for expensive firms, which was the design feature that made the multiplicative architecture HML-neutral.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: InvestedCapitalDislocationQuality
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The dislocation that accounting quality should be conditioned on belongs to the *business*, not to the levered equity stub: comparing book invested capital (equity plus net debt) with the market value of that same invested capital measures how cheaply the whole enterprise trades relative to its own history, free of leverage amplification.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly identified a numerator/denominator mismatch in the previous version — book equity over enterprise value mechanically penalizes levered firms — so this puts net invested capital in both numerator and denominator, which is the coherent capital-level analogue of book-to-market. Since leverage is the last known contaminant of the own-history anchor after the soft-asset purification worked (fmb 3.10, Sharpe 0.45), this tests whether de-levering the dislocation measure further sharpens the interaction while keeping dense balance-sheet coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HardBookChronicAccrualLevel
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Direction of working-capital intensity and the chronic *magnitude* of annual accruals are different facts: a firm can be tightening its ratio while still booking large accruals every year, so a dislocated-cheap firm is credible only when its average annual accrual per dollar of sales is small as well as falling.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the payout channel — which the critic rightly judged a payer dummy and weak evidence about earnings, since distributions can be debt-financed — with the accrual flow itself, averaged over five years so it measures habitual reliance rather than the single-year change that failed early in the archive. Both legs come from densely reported balance-sheet items under the purified hard-book anchor, so coverage should hold near 0.10 where the study's evidence has been reliable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapitalDislocationLevelAndTrend
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Credible cheapness requires accruals that are both small in habitual magnitude and falling in intensity; the chronic five-year average accrual per dollar of sales and the direction of working-capital intensity are separate facts, and neither the depreciation leg nor the trend alone captures the former.
considered.reasoning: The chronic-level channel produced alpha +3.2% (t 2.74, Sharpe 0.36) when paired with the hard-book anchor, and it avoids the asset-growth confound that the critic repeatedly flagged in the depreciation-intensity leg, so pairing it with the strongest anchor tests a quality composite that is entirely working-capital-based but spans magnitude and direction. It is the most economically pure statement of the value-trap mechanism the study has assembled.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapitalDislocationAccrualShareOfProfit
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), ADD(ABS(ib), dp)), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: The value-trap story is literally about the *share of reported profit that is accrual rather than cash*, so the right quality measure deflates accruals by the firm's earnings capacity rather than by sales or assets: a dislocated-cheap firm whose accruals consume a small fraction of its profit is reporting cash-backed income.
considered.reasoning: Every accrual leg in this study has been deflated by sales or assets, which measures accrual intensity of *activity*; deflating by earnings capacity measures accrual intensity of *reported profit*, which is the quantity the hypothesis is actually about and which reorders firms with high accruals but very high profits differently from firms with modest accruals and no profits. Using ABS(ib) plus depreciation in the denominator keeps the ratio finite for loss-makers and near-zero-earnings firms, the failure mode that makes naive accrual-to-earnings ratios explode.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OneSidedAccrualPenaltyCheap
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(MAX(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5), SUB(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5), TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)))), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The mechanism is one-sided: building working capital destroys the credibility of cheap earnings, but shrinking it faster and faster adds no further information once the firm is already releasing capital, so the penalty should apply only to the positive part of the accrual trend.
considered.reasoning: Every quality leg tested so far is linear in the accrual state, which implicitly assumes ever-greater working-capital contraction is ever-better news — economically doubtful, since aggressive liquidation is a distress symptom, not a quality signal. Truncating the trend at zero is a genuine functional-form claim about the mechanism rather than a new input, and pairing it with the depreciation leg inside SUMRANK breaks the tie mass created among all firms whose working capital is already falling.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OperatingCapitalDislocationQuality
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(at, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Cheapness should compare the book value of the *operating* capital a firm employs — assets excluding cash, net of non-debt operating liabilities — with the market value of exactly that operating capital, so the anchor measures how cheaply the market prices the productive asset base whose accounting quality the second leg audits.
considered.reasoning: The critic correctly showed the previous version's numerator collapsed to non-current assets while its denominator priced all operating assets, a base mismatch; defining the numerator as net operating assets and the denominator as enterprise value net of cash puts both sides on the same operating-capital base. This makes the anchor the direct book-to-market of the operating business, which is the object the accrual channels measure, rather than a mixture of equity, cash and leverage effects.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapitalDislocationHabitAcrossSystems
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(TS_SUM(SIGN(NEG(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), 5), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Accounting conservatism shows up as habit in the short-cycle accounts and as adequacy in the long-lived accounts: a de-levered dislocated firm that has repeatedly released working capital *and* charges depreciation at a rising rate is conservative in both accounting systems.
considered.reasoning: The previous version paired the sign count with the working-capital trend, two transformations of the same series, which the critic rightly judged mechanically redundant; replacing the partner leg with depreciation intensity puts the two legs in different parts of the balance sheet with genuinely different measurement errors. The count is also outlier-robust, which complements the slope leg's sensitivity to a single distorted fiscal year.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapitalDislocationTaxKeepingPaceWithSales
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), 5), ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), MA(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Real profits create real tax obligations: when accrued taxes keep growing in step with revenue, the reported income is being recognized by the tax authority as well as by management, whereas revenue growth unaccompanied by growing tax accruals is a signature of book-only earnings.
considered.reasoning: The tax channel has repeatedly moved the cross-sectional slope but only as a stale, size- and industry-confounded *level* (txp/at); expressing it as the change in accrued taxes per dollar of sales makes it a flow measure of tax verification that scales with the business, which is a different and better-specified variable rather than a reweighting. Paired at half weight with the working-capital slope under the study's best anchor, it targets the joint fmb-and-alpha objective with dense, well-populated inputs.

critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially Desai-Rajan-Sloan (2004) CFO/P — the published construct shown to subsume both value and accruals — and the two rank components share `oancf`, so the composite double-counts cash flow rather than combining two independent channels.

The internal logic and expected sign are consistent, but "value premium concentrated in low-accrual/high-cash-conversion firms" is a well-documented double sort, and a rank product is nearly monotone in a rank sum, so it adds little beyond proposal 1 beyond a cosmetic functional-form change.

The stated mechanism ("neutralizing cheap-and-accrual-heavy firms at zero") contradicts what the expression does — since BM is almost always positive, all gated-off firms fall to the bottom of the cross-section, making the short leg a pure accrual-heavy portfolio irrespective of valuation, plus the huge mass point at zero destabilizes quantile breakpoints.

A coherent, single-ratio construction with an independent balance-sheet measurement path, but EBITDA minus working-capital accrual is approximately pre-tax, pre-interest operating cash flow, so it is economically close to CFO/P, and dividing an unlevered flow by levered equity market cap (rather than EV) injects a leverage tilt that should be acknowledged.

Sign conventions on `recch`/`invch` are handled correctly and the sales-yield-plus-cash-conversion pairing is a reasonably distinct measurement route, but these cash-flow-statement line items are missing for a large share of firm-years and COALESCE-to-zero silently assigns those firms a median-ish quality rank, so coverage and the composition of the extreme buckets need checking.

Using accrual *instability* rather than accrual level is the most genuinely distinct idea in this batch and is internally consistent, though it must be verified that VOL's 5-period window spans five fiscal years (not five months of stale annual data), and the accrual-volatility leg may partly proxy known earnings-volatility/idiosyncratic-risk effects.

The multiplicative conditioning is a genuine architectural change from the archive's additive value+working-capital composite and correctly implements the "both legs equally cheap" HML-neutral design, but the ingredients are the same two well-worn ones (book-to-market, one-year balance-sheet working-capital accrual) and using `wcap` rather than non-cash working capital means cash accumulation is mislabeled as an accrual build.

Because depreciation typically dominates the working-capital change, the numerator is usually negative and the signal collapses to roughly −dp/ME, so the sort is driven by capital intensity scaled by market cap (a size/value bet) rather than by accrual quality, making the stated hypothesis inconsistent with what the expression actually computes — and market-deflated accruals ("percent/price-scaled accruals") are already a published variant.

This is the most substantively new idea in the batch — it swaps the exhausted working-capital channel for the long-lived-asset (depreciation adequacy) channel, industry-ranks the leg to strip the capital-intensity confound, and keeps the conditional structure that preserves HML-neutrality; the main risk is that dp/at proxies asset age and vintage as much as accounting conservatism.

Extending the accrual leg from a one-year flow to a five-year trend is a legitimate temporal test that is not in the archive, but `wcap` includes cash and short-term debt, so a cheap firm steadily building cash relative to sales gets shorted as a "value trap," which contradicts the hypothesis and dilutes the mechanism.

Changing only the deflator is a clean, well-motivated diagnostic of whether the parent signal's negative FF5 alpha was a leverage artifact, but the result is very close to the published enterprise-multiple (EBITDA/TEV, and effectively operating-cash-flow/EV) anomaly, so a large FF5 alpha is unlikely and coverage remains thin.

This is an unconditional additive stack of two long-published anomalies (dividend yield and Sloan accruals) with no genuine interaction, it repeats the SUMRANK architecture that already delivered negative FF5 alpha in the archive, and COALESCE(dvc,0) puts a large tie mass of non-payers at the bottom of one rank leg so the "valuation" component degenerates into a payer dummy/quality tilt.

A defensible but narrow refinement of the archived CheapWithFallingWorkingCapitalTrend — removing cash and short-term debt from the accrual leg is economically correct and non-cosmetic, but the two constructs will be highly correlated so the incremental information from the test is limited.

Internally consistent and it does open a non-working-capital accrual channel, but TREND(dp/at) is heavily confounded by the denominator — a rising ratio largely reflects shrinking or non-growing assets, so this risks being a repackaged asset-growth/investment anomaly interacted with B/M rather than a depreciation-conservatism signal.

Genuinely novel decomposition of CFO into earned versus liability-financed cash with a correctly signed quality leg (apalch/txach positive = cash inflow from stretching payables, negated), though COALESCE-to-zero on two sparsely populated cash-flow lines will inject measurement noise and should be checked against coverage.

The second-moment framing is a real addition to an archive dominated by accrual levels and slopes, but accrual volatility is close to the published Dechow–Dichev/Francis accrual-quality construct, and a 5-year VOL of a sales-deflated ratio is noisy enough that a weak result will be hard to interpret.

RANK is a monotone cross-sectional transform, so the sorted portfolios, ls_alpha, ls_talpha and ls_sharpe are identical to the archived signal by construction and only the FMB slope scale changes — this is a functional-form diagnostic, not a signal, and it does not merit an evaluation slot.

The MIN/Leontief conjunction is a structurally distinct interaction from the SUMRANK and product forms already in the archive and tests a falsifiable claim about complementarity, with the caveat that MIN of two ranks is mechanically correlated with their average and the short leg will be a heterogeneous mix of cheap-but-dirty and clean-but-expensive firms.

This is a single-deflator swap on the archive's already-tested CheapWithFallingWorkingCapitalTrend, and the proposal itself frames the likely outcome as a null, so it is a cosmetic variant offering diagnostic commentary rather than new return-predictive content (and trend-in-wcap/at is close to the published working-capital accrual anomaly).

The expression is internally consistent with the hypothesis and the two accounting-quality channels are economically distinct, but it is a straightforward rank-average of two already-archived amplifiers, so upside is limited to noise reduction rather than a new mechanism.

The algebra checks out (oancf − ib − dp ≈ negative working-capital accrual, so higher values mean better cash conversion, matching the positive expected sign), and the multi-year cumulative cash-flow-statement construction is a substantively different "state" measure from the archive's balance-sheet slopes.

Testing convexity of the amplifier with a hard B/M>1 gate is a genuinely untried design dimension and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the deep-value subsample's share of the cross-section is strongly time-varying, so portfolio composition instability and effective-coverage collapse are real risks that must be checked before believing any alpha.

It resurrects a channel that failed on every metric (fmb 0.08) by changing two things at once — the amplifier and a 3-year moving average — on sparse cash-flow lines, so it is a confounded, largely cosmetic patch that cannot attribute any result to either repair.

The haircut (three years of working-capital accruals) is typically small relative to book equity, so the signal will correlate near-perfectly with plain book-to-market — i.e. a rediscovery of HML that the archive has already shown produces negative FF5 alpha — and the proposal offers no evidence the reordering is large enough to matter.

A defensible incremental extension of the best archive signal, but the third leg (distance of non-cash WC/sales from its own 5-year max) is mechanically close to the negative 5-year slope of wcap/sales already in the composite, so the claimed independence is doubtful, and the nested SUMRANK silently weights the legs 1/2-1/4-1/4 rather than equally as the hypothesis implies.

The motivation is genuinely diagnostic — pairing a high-fmb/low-alpha leg (accrued taxes) with a high-alpha/low-fmb leg — but it remains a third-leg substitution in an existing composite, the nested SUMRANK weights the tax channel only 1/4, and txp is sparsely/zero-reported in ways that may mix a "reports the item at all" effect into the quality score.

Replacing the amplifier with a book-plus-sales value composite is a substantive rather than cosmetic change and is well-argued (B/M misprices asset-light and write-down firms), but sales-to-price is itself a long-known anomaly and the archive already showed sales-yield constructions producing negative FF5 alpha, so the expected improvement is speculative.

This is the first time-series valuation dimension in the study, is internally consistent (high TS_RANK of B/M = cheap versus own history = positive expected sign) and plausibly orthogonal to HML, though with annual data a 5-period TS_RANK is a very coarse, noisy amplifier that may blunt the interaction.

Squaring an already-uniform cheapness rank is a near-cosmetic monotone reweighting of the exact interaction already tested as CheapTwoChannelAccrualState, and it does not implement the claimed nonlinearity in any economically distinct way — it merely tilts the signed product toward high-B/M names, so any change in results will be uninterpretable scaling noise rather than evidence about convexity.

The second derivative of non-cash working-capital intensity is a genuinely new temporal concept relative to the levels, one-year changes, slopes, peak-distance and volatility already tested, and the sign is consistent; the main risks are that acceleration on annual data is very noisy and that the expression rewards a flattening *decline* as well as the intended decelerating build, which is not what the hypothesis describes.

A legitimate but incremental merge of the archive's two best gen-4 components (the TS_RANK cheapness amplifier and the WC/depreciation/tax quality composite) with no new mechanism, and the nested SUMRANK still buries the tax leg at quarter weight — the very defect its own reasoning cites elsewhere.

Averaging the cross-sectional and own-history cheapness amplifiers, both already tested with the identical quality leg, will almost mechanically interpolate between BroadValueAmplifiedQuality and OwnHistoryCheapWithQuality — and since the cross-sectional value ranks have repeatedly delivered *negative* FF5 alphas in this archive, blending them in is more likely to dilute the stronger incumbent than to teach anything.

This is a pure reweighting/ablation of QualityCompositeWithTaxCheck using only legs already in the archive, and while dropping the weak depreciation channel is a defensible diagnostic, it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different hypothesis, and it discards the TS_RANK amplifier that carried all of the portfolio evidence.

Genuinely the broadest untested accrual channel here — total net operating assets per dollar of sales spans capitalization and long-lived-asset decisions that every prior working-capital or depreciation leg misses — though it overlaps materially with the published net-operating-assets and asset-growth anomalies, so the incremental content beyond a plain NOA scalar should be checked.

One-year growth in book-to-market is dominated almost entirely by the past year's price change, so this is a disguised annual-reversal/negative-momentum bet whose positive expected sign runs against the well-documented momentum effect that FF5 does not span, meaning any alpha would be a known-factor artifact rather than the claimed "quality-validated sentiment markdown"; GROWTH is also ill-behaved for negative or near-zero ceq.

The all-time-series construction is a defensible and genuinely distinct design choice given the persistent negative alphas on cross-sectional yield legs, but with only five annual observations both TS_RANK legs take a handful of discrete values, producing coarse, lumpy sortings, and the second leg is close to a robustness restatement of the already-tested non-cash-WC-intensity trend.

This is a weight-reshuffling of channels already tested individually and jointly in the archive (ThreeChannelQualityCheap, QualityCompositeWithTaxCheck, OwnHistoryCheapSalesOutpacingAssets), and the premise that nesting order will transplant one leg's fmb onto another leg's alpha is a metric-fitting rationale rather than an economic one.

The hypothesis explicitly claims a conjunction ("cheap on *both* anchors") but the expression averages the two TS_RANKs, which permits one strong anchor to compensate for a weak one; moreover both anchors share the same price denominator and are already-tested legs, so the incremental information is likely small.

Changing the TS_RANK window from 5 to 10 on the archive's best signal while holding everything else fixed is a lookback parameter sweep, not a new mechanism, and the annual-data history requirement will materially shrink already-thin ~10% coverage and bias the sample toward long-lived survivors.

Shortening both quality slopes from 5 to 3 years is the mirror-image parameter tweak of the previous proposal, and a TREND over three annual observations is close to a noisy first difference — a horizon already shown to fail in the archive's one-year quality legs.

The claimed repair is likely misdiagnosed — the earlier 0% coverage almost certainly came from NaN propagation through MIN over the txp leg, which reordering ZSCORE inside MIN does not fix — and the "untested" conjunction claim is false since WeakestLinkCheapAndClean already implemented a MIN-of-ranks version.

Non-articulation between balance-sheet-derived and cash-flow-derived accruals is a genuinely distinct accounting-reliability channel (not the accrual magnitude already tested), the expression correctly computes the discrepancy and its sign matches the stated hypothesis; the main risk to check is that the measure mostly proxies for M&A/discontinued-operations activity rather than earnings quality.

This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive variants (BothAnchorsCheapWithQuality and NoRedFlagQualityOwnHistoryCheap) with no new economic content, and it will be near-collinear with both incumbents while further compressing the effective cross-section through double MIN-truncation.

The escape-route logic is coherent, but the added net-operating-asset leg is largely nested in the working-capital leg it is supposed to police (act ⊂ at, same operating-liability term), so the third hurdle mostly re-vetoes the same firms and the proposal reads as an incremental leg-count variant on an existing conjunction.

Substituting the weak depreciation-adequacy leg with a post-depreciation cash-margin trend is a genuine channel change rather than a reweighting, the sign logic is internally consistent, and the only real risk is the oancf-driven coverage drop to roughly 7% that should be reported as a diagnostic.

The diagnosis that a six-valued integer consistency count cannot support a cross-sectional level slope is plausible and the SUMRANK repair is targeted, though the two legs both measure working-capital release and are correlated enough that the gain may be modest.

Deviation-from-own-mean is a defensible normalization not yet tested in this form and the sign direction matches the expression, but it is conceptually close to the archive's TS_MAX "accrual unwind" and TS_RANK own-history variants, and the claim that it "keeps magnitude information" is partly undone by the outer cross-sectional RANK.

This is essentially a re-run of ConjunctiveQualityOwnHistoryCheap, whose txp-in-MIN structure already returned 0% coverage — wrapping ZSCORE around RANK does nothing to stop NaN propagation — and the cited fmb of 3.87 belongs to a four-way composite, not to the tax leg itself.

This is a pure 2x2 recombination of two archive signals (HardBookDislocationCleanCheap and OwnHistoryCheapWithQuality) differing by a single operator swap (MIN→SUMRANK), which is exactly the cosmetic-variant consolidation the objective warns against and adds no new economic claim.

The stated mechanism — strip leverage amplification to price the *business* — is not what the expression computes, since it puts book *equity* over *enterprise* value, a numerator/denominator mismatch that mechanically penalizes levered firms rather than neutralizing leverage (the coherent version would use invested capital or total assets in the numerator).

A legitimately motivated coverage repair that re-derives the highest-alpha quality channel from densely reported balance-sheet items, though the two legs (count of WC decreases and the WC/sales trend) are built from the same underlying series and are likely substantially redundant, which caps the expected information gain.

Testing the second moment of the accrual process alongside its trend is an economically distinct dimension (Dechow-Dichev-style accrual quality) that has only been tested under a contaminated amplifier, so the retest is defensible — but both legs derive from the same non-cash-WC/sales series, so the added dimension may be largely mechanical rather than informational.

Equal-weighting the externally verified tax leg is a substantively different quality channel with independent prior Fama-MacBeth support and an untested weighting, though the txp/at level is a stale, industry- and size-confounded proxy for tax verification and this remains one of three near-identical hard-book/SUMRANK cells proposed in the same batch.

MA(COALESCE(dvc,0)/at,3) is dominated by the payer/non-payer split, making the quality leg effectively a dividend-payer dummy and the signal a rediscovery of the well-documented payout/dividend-premium-in-value effect; moreover dividends can be debt-financed, so they are weak evidence that *earnings* are cash-backed.

This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested tweaks (standardized dislocation from StandardizedDislocationCleanCheap and the invested-capital anchor from InvestedCapitalDislocationQuality) with an identical quality leg, so it is closer to a cosmetic recombination than a new mechanism, and standardizing by a five-annual-observation VOL of a ratio whose denominator can shrink or flip sign when net cash is large adds fragility rather than information.

The expression is internally consistent and cheap to test, but it merely fills the remaining cell of an aggregation-rule × anchor grid already populated by NoRedFlagQualityOwnHistoryCheap and HardBookDislocationCleanCheap, contributing no new economic claim beyond "try MIN with the other anchor."

Still incremental — it swaps the anchor of the archived HardBookChronicAccrualLevel — but it makes the clearest surviving economic distinction (chronic accrual magnitude versus direction of intensity), deliberately drops the depreciation-intensity leg whose asset-growth confound was flagged, and the sign direction matches the expression.

Algebraically the cash term cancels in the numerator (ceq − NWC + net debt ≈ ceq + dltt − wcap ≈ noncurrent assets), so the numerator excludes both cash and working capital while the denominator is an enterprise value that prices all operating assets including working capital — a numerator/denominator base mismatch that directly contradicts the stated "cash and long-lived capital valued against the market value of the same capital base."

The two "independent" quality legs — a five-year sign count of negative ΔNWC and the five-year trend in wcap/sale — are near-mechanical duplicates of the same underlying series, so the claimed character-versus-momentum distinction is not supported, and everything else is a copy of BalanceSheetConsistencyPlusDirection with a different anchor.

A self-admitted no-new-economics rank average of two archived signals that share identical quality inputs (WC-intensity trend and depreciation-intensity trend) and highly correlated anchors, so the diversification premise fails and any gain would be an averaging artifact rather than evidence for a mechanism.
